glossary.definition: A machine-based system that infers, from given inputs, how to generate outputs (predictions, content, recommendations, decisions) that influence environments.
AI systems that pursue goals with a degree of autonomy, often using tools, memory, and delegation to take actions in a digital or physical environment.
An attack that manipulates an LLM through crafted inputs, including indirect injection via content consumed from tools or documents, to alter its behavior.
Adversarial manipulation of training data to degrade, bias, or backdoor model behavior.
An attack that reconstructs model behavior (or even weights) through queries, enabling theft or further attacks.
Under the EU AI Act, AI systems in specified high-impact use cases that must meet mandatory requirements before deployment.
General-Purpose AI model - a model with significant generality that can perform a wide range of tasks, subject to specific EU AI Act obligations.
A catalog of all AI systems and models used by an organization, forming the basis for risk assessment and governance.
Adversarial testing by a team that simulates attacks to identify vulnerabilities in AI systems before release.
Degradation of model performance over time due to changes in input data distribution or environment.
